sessions.title: Welcome
sessions.set_the_stage:
Welcome to Just Build. Over today you will go from never having built an agent to designing and watching a real one run, on a real problem. No coding background needed.

Here is the shape of the day: what an agent actually is, then the thinking behind a good one, then you do a real task by hand, design the agent for it, and watch it run.

Screens down and eyes up when we are talking; screens up when we are doing. Let's build.

sessions.title: Agents in the Real World: A Practitioner's View
sessions.set_the_stage:
We open with the practitioner's view. Before we touch any code, we answer the questions a working professional actually asks: what is an agent, where does it help, where does it fall down, and how do we keep it safe.

I'll walk you through these slides one idea at a time, with a wrong way and a right way for each. We'll slow down on the risks and on keeping a human in the loop; that is the grown-up part of this conversation.

By the end, you should be able to say in one sentence what an agent reads, decides, and produces, and name the one place it could quietly go wrong.

sessions.title: The Humanics of AI
sessions.set_the_stage:
This is the thinking layer, and it is where the real skill lives. The best agent-builders are not the fastest typists; they are the clearest thinkers. We'll work through first principles, systems thinking, decomposition, and how to define what good even means.

None of this is abstract. Every habit here points straight at the recruitment agent we build next. Breaking a task into atoms, seeing the whole pipe, and framing a sharp question are exactly what will make that agent easy to design.

Take these seriously and the build becomes the easy part. The clear thinking is what you'll carry into every agent you ever make.

sessions.title: Recruit by Hand
sessions.set_the_stage:
Before we build anything, you will do the recruitment job by hand. Here is your problem: 25 resumes and one job description, and time to interview only five people. Shortlist the best five yourselves.

This is where you learn what 'good' really looks like, and where your own judgement lives. Set your criteria before you read, score every resume on the same grid, and be able to say why each of your five made it.

The five you pick, with your reasons, become the yardstick we hold the agent to next. The cleaner your by-hand answer, the sharper the agent you design.

sessions.title: Design the Agentic Logic
sessions.set_the_stage:
Now we turn what you just did by hand into an agent, on paper, before any code. Box by box, we convert your own process into the agent's logic.

The facts you read become the extract. Your scoring grid becomes the code. The disqualifier you applied without even thinking becomes the hard rule. Your shortlist, with reasons, becomes a draft that a human approves.

When the design is right, the code is just typing it out. By the end you will have designed a complete agent, from your own hands, on a single page.

sessions.title: Watch Me Run the Recruitment Agent
sessions.set_the_stage: You designed the recruitment agent on paper. Now we run it, live. First we cover where it runs: what Google Colab is, and what a Gemini key is and why it matters. Then I open the notebook and drive, and you watch the three agents you designed work on the exact 25 resumes you ranked by hand. At the end, we lay the agent's five next to your five, and that is how you learn to trust it.

sessions.title: Summary of Day 1
sessions.set_the_stage: That is the whole of day one. Before you head out, we look back at everything you learned, then forward to the shape of day two. You started not knowing what an agent was; you leave having designed one and watched it run on a real problem. Tomorrow, you build your own.

sessions.title: Start of Day 2
sessions.set_the_stage: Welcome back. Yesterday you learned what an agent is, did the work by hand, designed it, and watched it run. Today the problem is yours: you pick it, design the agent, and run it yourself, start to finish. Same method as yesterday, now in your hands.

build.title: Pick from the palette
build.instructions: Choose the use-case closest to your world. Same three agents, different job.

build.title: Change only the marked lines
build.instructions: You'll swap the documents, the extract fields, the rubric, and the hard rule. Everything else stays exactly as it is.

build.title: Run it on the fallback
build.instructions: Leave the fallback switch on. It runs on saved results so nothing blocks you. Flip it off only if you want to go live on your own key.

build.title: Defend one choice
build.instructions: Pair up and justify one design choice to another pair: why that criterion, why that weight, why that hard rule. Building is shallow; defending is deep.

sessions.title: Build Your Own Agent
sessions.set_the_stage:
Now I'll hand over the notebook to you. You'll pick one use-case from the palette, from finops, support, sales, and more, and configure the exact same three-agent design for it. You only change the marked lines.

This run defaults to the fallback switch, so it works with zero friction even if the free tier hiccups. I'll say it plainly: you already learned the live key this morning, so this run is about the pattern, not the plumbing. The live path is one flip away if you want it.

The point here is ownership. When you watch the same machine work on a problem from your own world, that is when it truly clicks.

sessions.title: The Valuenomics of AI
sessions.set_the_stage:
Now we talk value. A working agent is not the prize; the outcome is. We'll trace the chain from data to insight to narrative to influence to outcome, and see how the same shape unlocks value across domains.

Then we'll widen the toolbox beyond the screen-and-rank agent you built, into the other patterns you'll meet out there, each with a place it genuinely wins.

The thread running through all of it: the honest, defensible story you can tell a recruiter, built on a real agent and a real number you measured yourself.

build.title: Name your next agent
build.instructions: Pick one boring, repeated, judgement-based task in your own life and commit to building an agent for it this week.

build.title: Start your portfolio
build.instructions: Save every agent you build, each with its before-and-after number. That folder is your proof, and it grows from today.

sessions.title: What Next
sessions.set_the_stage:
We close on the road ahead. You walked in curious and you leave able to build; this session is about what you do with that.

We'll talk about how to spot opportunities, how to keep building, how to turn this into something real, placements, freelance, even a venture, and the mindset that outlasts any single tool.

End it on one concrete commitment: the one agent each of you will build this week. Momentum from here is everything.

ideas.name: FinOps · Invoicing
ideas.for_whom: You, if FinOps or Finance is your world.
ideas.agent2: Check against purchase orders, policy and duplicates
ideas.agent3: Draft an approval recommendation, or flag exceptions for a human

ideas.name: Customer Ops · Customer Requests
ideas.for_whom: You, if Customer Ops or Support is your world.
ideas.agent1: Extract the customer's issue and intent
ideas.agent2: Classify by type and urgency, and prioritise
ideas.agent3: Draft a reply and route to the right team, behind a human check

ideas.name: IT Ops · Ticket Triage
ideas.for_whom: You, if IT Operations is your world.
ideas.agent1: Extract the reported fault and system
ideas.agent2: Classify priority and likely cause, and prioritise
ideas.agent3: Draft first-response steps and route to the right IT team

ideas.name: Sales Ops · Lead Qualification
ideas.for_whom: You, if Sales Ops or Revenue is your world.
ideas.agent1: Extract the prospect's needs and fit signals
ideas.agent3: Draft a personalised follow-up and assign the next action
